jp: 水[みず]を{入[い]れると/入[い]れれば|cd-to}、この粉[こな]はすぐにスープになります。
en: If you add water, this powder turns into soup right away.
why: A natural result that always follows an action is expressed with と.

jp: 夜[よる]、スーパーに{行[い]くと/行[い]ったら|cd-to}、お弁当[べんとう]が半額[はんがく]になっていた。
en: When I went to the supermarket at night, the bento boxes had been marked half price.
why: Going and discovering something is a past discovery, which takes と.

jp: 春[はる]に{なると/なれば|cd-to}、近所[きんじょ]の店[みせ]にいちごがたくさん並[なら]びます。
en: When spring comes, lots of strawberries line the shelves of the neighborhood shops.
why: A regular event that follows a change of season takes と.

jp: レジで千円[せんえん]札[さつ]を{出[だ]すと/出[だ]したら|cd-to}、店員[てんいん]は小銭[こぜに]のおつりをくれた。
en: When I handed over a thousand-yen note at the register, the clerk gave me change in coins.
why: An action followed by a fact in the past is reported with と; ば and なら cannot.

jp: ポイントカードを{出[だ]すと/出[だ]せば|cd-to}、会計[かいけい]が一割[いちわり]安[やす]くなる。
en: If you show the point card, the bill becomes ten percent cheaper.
why: A rule that always holds after an action takes と.

jp: 値札[ねふだ]をよく{見[み]ると/見[み]たら|cd-to}、三百円[さんびゃくえん]ではなく三千円[さんぜんえん]だった。
en: When I looked closely at the price tag, it was three thousand yen, not three hundred.
why: Looking and discovering a fact is a discovery, which takes と.
